name: Minister's Special Licence (MSL) Resident Draw Grants
summary: Alberta Conservation Association grants, funded by Government of Alberta special hunting licence draws, for projects that conserve and enhance wildlife populations and their habitat in Alberta. Organisations and individuals can lead.
reporting: A final report is due March 15 of the project year, with a signed financial statement.

eligibility.rule: Project takes place in and relates to Alberta
Be a legally recognized organization or individual with required coverage
Lead applicant is not a federal or provincial ministry or its employee
Project activities occur between April 1, 2027 and March 31, 2028
Do not claim funding for work started before April 1, 2027
Not for profit-making, overhead, deficit financing, fundraising or land purchase
Obtain all licences and approvals required for the project

Applicants will be notified of status of their submission by March 31, 2027.
Successful grant applicants will be expected to sign and follow the ACA Cooperative Project Agreement

eligibility.quote: MSLRDG only funds projects that occur in, and relate to, Alberta.
Any legally recognized organization (charity/society/corporation) or individual, with appropriate liability insurance and WCB coverage, can apply

MSLRDG does not fund applications where the federal or provincial government employee is the principal applicant (principal applicant is considered the lead on a project) or the principal applicant is a federal or provincial ministry.
Project activities must occur between April 1, 2027, and March 31, 2028.
Grants cannot be made retrospectively, that is for work started prior to the current fiscal year (i.e., before April 1, 2027).
Projects outside of Alberta. Profit-making activities. Overhead costs. Emergency funds or deficit financing. General fundraising. Land acquisition.
Applicants are responsible for ensuring they have the proper licences and approvals required to carry out the project
